name: Dtag
description: Demand-rate tag system — Emil Post's tag system as a demand UGen. Reads symbols from an axiom array, applies production rules indexed by integer symbols, and deletes v symbols at each step. The tape size is bounded; recycle/mode controls behaviour on overrun and empty conditions. From sc3-plugins TagSystemUGens. Documented as a builder-only entry because the input list is variadic (axiom and rules arrays are flattened into the input vector).

inputs.name: .bufsize(size)
inputs.description: Maximum tape size; when this size is reached, the process ends (depending on mode)

inputs.name: .v(num)
inputs.description: Deletion number — symbols deleted at each step

inputs.name: .axiom(array)
inputs.description: Initial string of integer symbols (rule indices)

inputs.name: .rules(array_of_arrays)
inputs.description: Production rules — for each integer symbol, an array of replacement symbols

inputs.name: .recycle(offset)
inputs.description: If non-zero, write position is offset and the tag system recycles instead of halting (depending on mode)

inputs.name: .mode(m)
inputs.description: Halting/recycling mode (0..5) — see schelp for full table

name: DbufTag
description: Demand-rate tag system that runs on an external Buffer instead of a fixed-size internal tape. Like Dtag but uses Buffer.alloc, allowing multiple tag processes to share or overwrite each other's output on a single buffer. From sc3-plugins TagSystemUGens. Documented as a builder-only entry because the input list is variadic.

inputs.name: .bufnum(num)
inputs.description: Index of the 1-channel buffer used as the tag tape

inputs.name: .v(num)
inputs.description: Deletion number — symbols deleted at each step

name: Dfsm
description: Demand-rate finite-state machine — a Markov chain in UGen form. Each state holds a number of next-state choices; one is randomly selected per step from a user-provided RNG. Similar to Pfsm but evaluable as a UGen at demand rate. From sc3-plugins TagSystemUGens. Documented as a builder-only entry because the rules input is variadic and structured.

inputs.name: .rules(array)
inputs.description: Rules in the format [[entry states], item, [next states], item, [next states], ..., end item] — items can be numbers or demand UGens

inputs.name: .n(count)
inputs.description: Number of items to embed from each state, or inf to embed completely

inputs.name: .rgen(ugen)
inputs.description: Demand-rate RNG outputting values 0..1 — selects the next state. Deterministic UGens give controllable choice
